title: Cardiac arrest
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Recognise cardiac arrest and call the team and start compressions without delay.
Keep the pre-shock pause as short as possible.
Perform and call the safety check before a shock.
Know that defibrillator operation is limited to authorised roles.

sources.use: ERC ALS 2025 (paraphrase only; commercial use needs an agreement)
AHA adult ALS 2025: selected CPR and rhythm-specific defibrillation recommendations
AHA adult BLS 2025: recognition and early CPR

required_sources: Unit resuscitation policy and the authorised-role requirements
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.

Rhythm analysis, energy selection, drugs and post-arrest care remain outside this scenario. AHA 2025 BLS and ALS selected recommendations are linked; full appraisal and update/errata reconciliation remain outstanding.
Authorised-role requirements for defibrillation are local.

setting: A fictional adult found unresponsive on a fictional unit with a monitor and defibrillator.

steps.info: During an ICU observation round, an adult suddenly becomes unresponsive. Breathing is abnormal with occasional gasps. The arrest team has not yet been called and a definite pulse has not been established. A colleague is nearby.
steps.prompt: Which response minimizes delay to cardiac arrest recognition, emergency activation and CPR?

options.text: Activate the cardiac arrest response and start CPR without delay when arrest is confirmed or cannot promptly be excluded, following the local resuscitation pathway. Ask another team member to bring the defibrillator and provide trained ventilation support.
options.feedback: Unresponsiveness with absent or abnormal breathing requires rapid arrest recognition, emergency activation and CPR without avoidable delay. If a trained pulse check is part of the local pathway, it must not delay CPR. Gasping is not normal breathing. Follow the trained healthcare-professional pulse assessment pathway; if no definite pulse is found promptly, begin CPR.
options.consequence: Immediate activation and CPR when indicated may minimize time without effective circulation while colleagues bring equipment.

options.text: Fetch the defibrillator first and start compressions when you return.
options.feedback: Equipment is needed, but compressions should not wait for it.
options.consequence: Leaving to fetch equipment could delay chest compressions and emergency support.

options.text: Wait for a senior to arrive before doing anything.
options.feedback: Waiting delays treatment; call for help and start compressions.
options.consequence: Waiting for a senior could prolong the interruption to circulation.

steps.info: At the next shared checkpoint, CPR is in progress and the defibrillator has arrived. Pads have not yet been applied. The trained operator has not yet determined whether the rhythm is shockable.
steps.prompt: How should the team prepare for rhythm assessment while minimizing interruptions to compressions?

options.text: Apply pads promptly and continue CPR. The authorised manual-defibrillator operator or AED pathway determines whether a shock is indicated. If charging for an indicated shock, continue compressions where safe and minimise interruptions.
options.feedback: Not every arrest rhythm is shockable. Maintain CPR and use the trained rhythm-specific or AED pathway; avoid unnecessary pauses for an indicated shock.
options.consequence: Early pad placement and coordinated rhythm assessment may reduce avoidable interruptions to CPR.

options.text: Stop compressions until the defibrillator has charged.
options.feedback: Stopping while charging lengthens the pre-shock pause.
options.consequence: Stopping compressions before necessary rhythm analysis or shock delivery could prolong the pause.

options.text: Use the paddles without checking contact because they are quicker.
options.feedback: Pads are preferred; if paddles are used, firm force and good contact are needed.
options.consequence: Poor electrode contact could compromise safe and effective shock delivery.

steps.info: At the final shared checkpoint, the authorized operator has identified a shockable rhythm and an indicated shock is ready. Contact with the patient and bed has not yet been checked, and oxygen delivery equipment is nearby. There is no confirmed return of circulation.
steps.prompt: Which safety checks and immediate post-shock actions are required?

observations.label: Post-shock plan
observations.value: Resume CPR immediately unless team identifies reason to assess circulation

options.text: Visually confirm nobody is touching the patient or bed, manage oxygen safety according to the airway circuit and local protocol, and support delivery by the authorized operator. Resume CPR immediately after the indicated shock unless the team identifies a reason to assess return of circulation.
options.feedback: Use a visual and verbal safety check and distinguish free-flow oxygen from an attached ventilation circuit. After shock delivery, immediately resume chest compressions; do not routinely pause for a pulse check. The team may assess return of spontaneous circulation if clinical and physiological signs suggest it. Do not stop compressions solely because an isolated capnography value rises.
options.consequence: A visual safety check and prompt resumption of CPR may protect rescuers and limit interruption to resuscitation.

options.text: Deliver the shock while a colleague continues manual compressions, wearing gloves.
options.feedback: A shock must not be given during manual compressions, even with gloves.
options.consequence: Shock delivery during manual compressions could expose a rescuer to injury.

options.text: Shout 'clear' once without looking around the bed.
options.feedback: A verbal warning alone does not establish that rescuers are clear. The operator must visually verify safety before delivering an indicated shock.
options.consequence: A verbal warning without visual confirmation could leave someone in contact with the patient or bed.

learning_points: Call the team and start compressions without delay.
Confirm that a shock is indicated via the rhythm-specific or AED pathway, maintain CPR during preparation and minimise pauses.
Perform and call the safety check; never shock during manual compressions.
Resume CPR immediately after the indicated shock unless the trained team identifies clinical and physiological signs warranting assessment of return of circulation.
